## Install {#install} Requires R 4.1 or later. `matisseR` depends only on `data.table`; the other packages are for plotting. ```r install.packages(c("data.table", "ggplot2", "patchwork", "scales", "remotes")) remotes::install_github("filhoalm/matisseR") ``` The package source, issue tracker and README are at [github.com/filhoalm/matisseR](https://github.com/filhoalm/matisseR). Every function has a help page: for example `?apc_fit`. ## Function reference {#functions} The main functions, by the module that teaches them. | Function | What it does | Module | |---|---|---| | `matisse_example()` | Index and data of the eight synthetic example datasets | [0](modules/m0-welcome.qmd), [1](modules/m1-lexis-rates.qmd) | | `csv2rates()`, `rates2csv()` | Read and write the NCI Age Period Cohort Web Tool CSV format | [1](modules/m1-lexis-rates.qmd) | | `rates_make()` | Build a rates object from a table of cases and person-years | [1](modules/m1-lexis-rates.qmd) | | `rates_long()`, `rates_uni()` | A table with one row per Lexis cell; a one-line summary | [1](modules/m1-lexis-rates.qmd) | | `rates_chunk()` | Combine ages and periods into larger cells | [1](modules/m1-lexis-rates.qmd) | | `rates_fill()` | Replace zero or missing events with a small positive value | [1](modules/m1-lexis-rates.qmd) | | `rates_i5()`, `pchip()` | Interpolate 5-year age groups to single years; shape-preserving interpolation | [1](modules/m1-lexis-rates.qmd) | | `lexis_plot()` | Lexis diagram: age by period beside age by cohort | [1](modules/m1-lexis-rates.qmd) | | `apc_design()` | The age-period-cohort design matrix | [2](modules/m2-new-apc-model.qmd) | | `apc_fit()` | Fit the New APC model (weighted least squares or Poisson) | [2](modules/m2-new-apc-model.qmd) | | `apc_ef()`, `apc_efs()` | One or several estimable functions with 95% confidence limits | [2](modules/m2-new-apc-model.qmd) | | `apc_ref()`, `apc_scale()`, `apc_contrast()`, `apc_ef_vcov()` | Reference cells, scales, contrasts and covariance of an estimable function | [2](modules/m2-new-apc-model.qmd) | | `capricorn()` | Comparative APC analysis: five models, tests and AICc | [3](modules/m3-capricorn.qmd) | | `cap_ef()` | Estimable functions and rate ratios by group | [3](modules/m3-capricorn.qmd) | | `cap_map()`, `cap_fit()`, `cap_blocks()` | Building blocks of the comparative models | [3](modules/m3-capricorn.qmd) | | `social_generations()`, `generation_contrasts()` | Generations, proxy parents and the contrasts between them | [4](modules/m4-generations-shares.qmd) | | `apc_fcp()` | Fitted cohort pattern at any reference age | [4](modules/m4-generations-shares.qmd) | | `fcp_generations()`, `fcp_contrast()` | Mean fitted rate by generation; fitted cohort share | [4](modules/m4-generations-shares.qmd) | The generation and share functions go beyond the MATLAB toolbox. See [Module 5](modules/m5-matlab-methods.qmd) for the MATLAB methods that are not yet in R. ## Example datasets {#datasets} Eight synthetic Lexis diagrams: single years of age 35 to 84 by calendar years 1991 to 2019, with Poisson counts drawn from known age-period-cohort surfaces shaped like common cancer patterns. They are **not registry data**, and they are free to use under the package's MIT license. In R, call `matisse_example(i)`; here are the CSV files (NCI web tool format) for any other software. |Dataset |Site |Sex |Population |Cases | Zero cells|True net drift (%/yr) |Design | |:-------------------------|:-----------|:---|:----------|:-------|----------:|:---------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------| |[syn01_melanoma_F_A.csv](data/syn01_melanoma_F_A.csv)|melanoma |F |A |16,339 | 0|1.86 |main example: rising cohort pattern | |[syn02_melanoma_F_B.csv](data/syn02_melanoma_F_B.csv)|melanoma |F |B |9,905 | 4|3.09 |A with a different period trend (vs A: PH-X holds) | |[syn03_melanoma_F_C.csv](data/syn03_melanoma_F_C.csv)|melanoma |F |C |3,203 | 178|1.86 |A x 1.3 in a small population, zero cells (vs A: PH-A holds) | |[syn04_melanoma_F_D.csv](data/syn04_melanoma_F_D.csv)|melanoma |F |D |9,674 | 13|3.40 |A with a steeper cohort trend (vs A: PH-L holds) | |[syn05_breast_F_A.csv](data/syn05_breast_F_A.csv)|breast |F |A |113,679 | 0|0.66 |population A: steady cohort increase | |[syn06_lung_F_A.csv](data/syn06_lung_F_A.csv)|lung |F |A |34,885 | 9|0.32 |population A: cohort peak around 1948 | |[syn07_all_cancers_F_A.csv](data/syn07_all_cancers_F_A.csv)|all cancers |F |A |423,369 | 0|- |population A: examples 1, 5 and 6 plus other cancers (same person-years) | |[syn08_thyroid_M_C.csv](data/syn08_thyroid_M_C.csv)|thyroid |M |C |759 | 877|3.56 |small population, mostly zero cells, rising period trend | ## Slides and data preparation {#slides} Course slides, and the steps to prepare registry data for the NCI web tool (which `csv2rates()` reads directly). | File | Description | Size | |---|---|---| | [SEER_CI5plus_to_APC_WebTool.pptx](downloads/SEER_CI5plus_to_APC_WebTool.pptx) | From SEER\*Stat or the CI5 Plus database to the APC input matrix, and the rules the web tool enforces | 1.8 MB | | [Statistical_Methods_in_CSR.pptx](downloads/Statistical_Methods_in_CSR.pptx) | Statistical methods in cancer surveillance research: why these methods are needed | 1.0 MB | | [The_Lexis_Diagram.pptx](downloads/The_Lexis_Diagram.pptx) | The Lexis diagram, its axes, and comparing several diagrams | 3.1 MB | The [NCI Age Period Cohort Analysis Web Tool](https://analysistools.cancer.gov/apc/) runs the standard analysis in a browser. Its rules include equal age and period interval widths (5-year ages need 5-year periods) and no zero count or population cells. ## Method papers {#papers} - [Advances in statistical methods for cancer surveillance research: an age-period-cohort perspective](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/oncology/articles/10.3389/fonc.2023.1332429/full) (Front Oncol 2024; [PDF](downloads/Filho_Rosenberg_2024_FrontOncol.pdf)). The overview of the methods. - [The new age-period-cohort model](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0962280218801121) (Stat Methods Med Res). Module 2. - [Comparative age-period-cohort analysis](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12874-023-02039-8) (BMC Med Res Methodol 2023; [PDF](downloads/Rosenberg_2023_BMCMedResMethodol.pdf)). CAPRICORN and EPIPHANY; Module 3. - [Cancer incidence trends in successive social generations in the US](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2819747) (JAMA Netw Open 2024). Generations, proxy parents and SAGE; Module 4. - [Smoothing methods for Lexis diagrams](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/09622802231192950). SIFT; Module 5. - [A web tool for age-period-cohort analysis of cancer incidence and mortality rates](https://aacrjournals.org/cebp/article/23/11/2296/14669/A-Web-Tool-for-Age-Period-Cohort-Analysis-of) (Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2014). The NCI web tool. ## Glossary {#glossary} **Age-period-cohort (APC) analysis** : Statistical analysis of rates that separates the effects of age, calendar period and birth cohort. **Birth cohort** : People born in the same years. In a Lexis diagram, cohort = period - age. **CAPRICORN** : Comparative APC analysis: fits several groups together and tests whether their rates are proportional by age, period or cohort. **Estimable function (EF)** : A curve built from the model that does not depend on how the unidentifiable linear trend is assigned: LAC, CAC, FTT, FCP and local drifts. **Fitted cohort pattern (FCP)** : The model's rate at a reference age for each birth cohort. **Fitted temporal trend (FTT)** : The model's rate at a reference age for each calendar period. **Lexis diagram** : A grid of age by calendar period, holding events and person-years in each cell. **Local drift (LD)** : The annual percent change in the rate at each age. **Net drift** : The overall annual percent change in rates; the linear trend that cannot be assigned to period or cohort alone. **Overdispersion** : Variation in counts beyond what the Poisson distribution allows. Real counts usually show it; `capricorn(overdispersion = TRUE)` allows for it. **Person-years (offset)** : The population time at risk in a cell; the denominator of a rate. **Proxy parents** : The cohorts born 20 to 29 years before a generation's first and last birth years. **Rates object** : The `matisseR` representation of a Lexis diagram: matrices of events and person-years by age group and period. **Social generation** : A broad group of birth cohorts, such as the Baby Boomers (1946 to 1964). ## How to cite {#cite} If you use the methods, cite the overview paper and the paper for the method you used: - Filho A, Rosenberg PS. Advances in statistical methods for cancer surveillance research: an age-period-cohort perspective. *Front Oncol* 2024;13:1332429. [doi:10.3389/fonc.2023.1332429](https://doi.org/10.3389/fonc.2023.1332429) - Comparative APC (CAPRICORN): Rosenberg PS et al. *BMC Med Res Methodol* 2023 (PMID 37853346). - Social generations: Rosenberg PS, Filho A. *JAMA Netw Open* 2024. [doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.15731](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.15731) To cite the software: *matisseR: an R port of the MATISSE toolbox, version 0.1.0.* [github.com/filhoalm/matisseR](https://github.com/filhoalm/matisseR) Questions?
